toegepas.voor: ou geboue en ou potte en ou gereedskap
toegepas.na: ou geboue, ou potte en ou gereedskap
toegepas.rede_vinder: A list reads more naturally with commas and one 'en' before the last item.
toegepas.fout: The repeated 'en ... en' in a written list reads as unpolished speech in a study text.
toegepas.rede_keurder: A comma list with one 'en' is the natural written form; the items and meaning are unchanged, and change 3 keeps the two sentences parallel.

toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017 comma before 'en' joining two clauses that each have their own subject and verb.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS 2017 comma before 'en' joining two clauses with their own subject and verb.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Ou dinge kan breek' and 'ou stories kan ... wegraak' are each full clauses, so the comma is required.

toegepas.voor: en net so vorm wat ons vandag doen die toekoms
toegepas.na: en wat ons vandag doen, vorm net so die toekoms
toegepas.rede_vinder: The subject clause sitting between the verb and its object is hard to parse; fronting it reads clearly.
toegepas.fout: With the subject clause between 'vorm' and its object, a reader can first parse 'vorm wat ons vandag doen' as 'shapes what we do today'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Fronting the subject clause removes the misreading, mirrors the first half of the sentence, and keeps 'net so' and the meaning intact.

laat_vaar.voor: deur mense gebou wat lank voor jou gelewe het
laat_vaar.na: deur mense gebou wat lank gelede gelewe het
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Avoids repeating 'lank voor jou' from the previous sentence without changing the meaning.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The repeated 'lank voor jou' is a deliberate parallel that ties both sentences to the learner; 'lank gelede' loses that link and is only different, not better.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'kyk' with no object is unnatural here; the objects being looked at should be named by a pronoun.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'waar almal kan kyk' is natural Afrikaans, and swapping 'kyk' for 'sien' with an added object changes the verb's sense without fixing a fault.

na_skrywer.rede_vinder: Songs, stories and dances are 'oorgedra', not 'oorgegee', which suggests handing over an object.
na_skrywer.fout: 'oorgee' (hand over) is less idiomatic than 'oordra' for passing on songs, stories and dances.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: The point is real, but lesson 4's revised 'erfenis' glossary entry deliberately uses 'oorgee' to match this sentence, so changing only this lesson would split the shared picture; the writer must decide both lessons together.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer
